caveat: Partial correctness and model safety under the pinned 64-bit Go model, with package initialization and owned inputs as preconditions; compiler/runtime correctness, OOM and termination are excluded. Generated opaque type declarations remain and are reported by the theorem axiom sets. Complete all-input/all-owned-destination Header API composition is checked against independent HeaderFirstSpec/HeaderFullSpec, but requires Utf8ValidatorContract. The complete actual UTF-8 validator loop reduces that premise to Utf8WordWindowContract; the actual generic eight-byte helper remains unproved because the documented trusted slice-index repair is unapplied. Complete public BigInt decoding is now checked against independent integer success/rejection relations, with exact values, consumption, owned outputs/errors, input preservation and rollback; the pinned errors.Is comparability model is restricted here to concrete pointer targets. Relevant initialization establishes actual immutable tables and error-category objects after modeled runtime CPU startup. Resource-key map and transaction-interface witnesses are checked, but they are not payload decoder proofs; felt-key maps expose a separate array-equality modeling gap. Only Header currently has a registered typed reader; other production roots retain the original planner. The manifest and saved no-fallback corpus results are source-specific evidence, not formal fxamacker equivalence. Ignored CBOR text is intentionally not always validated, so successful decoding is not blanket RFC validity. No whole-library correctness or frozen performance-gate result is claimed.
